title: The Listening Tree

pages.text: Loyal Dog loved to talk! He could bark about his favorite stick for hours. But one day, his friend Gentle Deer was very quiet.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes being a good friend means being quiet and listening.

pages.text: 'Are you okay?' Dog asked. Then he did something hard — he stopped talking and just listened. Deer shared that she was feeling lonely.
pages.narratorLine: Generous Listening means giving someone your whole attention.

pages.text: After Deer finished, Dog said, 'Thank you for telling me.' A beautiful tree grew between them, its branches reaching wide. 'That's the Listening Tree,' said Deer. 'It grows when friends truly hear each other.'
pages.narratorLine: Can you be a generous listener today?

doAction.instruction: Practice generous listening — give someone your full attention.
steps: Find a friend or family member.
Listen without interrupting. Just listen with your whole heart.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Listen to someone tell you a story.

shinePrompt: What did you learn by listening?

title: The Welcome Path

pages.text: Sweet Skunk saw a new animal at the edge of the forest — a small hedgehog, curled up tight. 'Everyone stays away from me,' Hedgehog said sadly.
pages.narratorLine: Everyone deserves to feel like they belong.

pages.text: 'I know how that feels,' said Skunk softly. 'Some animals stay away from me too. But I know a secret — everyone belongs in this forest.'
pages.narratorLine: Sweet Skunk knows that being different is what makes us special.

pages.text: Skunk held out her paw. 'Come walk with me.' As they walked together, flowers bloomed along the path. The forest was more beautiful with everyone in it.
pages.narratorLine: Is there someone you could welcome today?

doAction.instruction: Welcome someone or include someone who might feel left out.
steps: Think of someone who might feel alone — at school, at the playground, or in your neighborhood.
Invite them to join you in something.
Make them feel like they belong.

shinePrompt: How did it feel to make someone feel welcome?

title: The Compliment Blossoms

pages.text: Loyal Dog discovered something magical in Friendship Forest — every kind word he said made a flower bloom!
pages.narratorLine: Kind words are powerful. They can change someone's whole day.

pages.text: 'You're a great climber!' he told Squirrel. Pop! A pink flower. 'You have the kindest smile!' he told Deer. Pop! A golden flower.
pages.narratorLine: A compliment is a gift you can give anytime, anywhere.

pages.text: Soon the whole forest was filled with colorful blossoms. 'I didn't know my words could do all this,' Dog said in wonder. 'Kind words always grow,' said Squirrel.
pages.narratorLine: Ready to grow some flowers of your own? Give three compliments today!

doAction.instruction: Give three genuine compliments to three different people.
steps: Think about what you appreciate about three people.
Tell each one something kind and specific.
Watch how it makes them feel!

shinePrompt: How did people react to your kind words?

title: The Sorry Bridge

pages.text: Gentle Deer accidentally stepped on a beautiful mushroom that Squirrel had been growing. 'Oh no,' Deer gasped. Squirrel's eyes filled with tears.
pages.narratorLine: Sometimes we hurt people even when we don't mean to.

pages.text: 'I'm so sorry,' said Deer. 'I know that mushroom was special to you. I should have been more careful.' She didn't make excuses. She just felt sorry, truly.
pages.narratorLine: A real apology means understanding how the other person feels.

pages.text: Squirrel sniffled, then smiled. 'Thank you for saying that.' Together they planted a new mushroom. Where the old one broke, a little bridge grew, connecting their two favorite trees.
pages.narratorLine: Sorry isn't just a word — it's a bridge back to each other.

doAction.instruction: If you've hurt someone's feelings recently, say a genuine sorry.
steps: Think about whether you've hurt someone recently, even by accident.
Tell them you're sorry and say what you're sorry for.
Ask if there's something you can do to help.
doAction.seedlingSimplified: Practice saying 'I'm sorry' with a grown-up.

shinePrompt: What did you learn about apologies?

title: The Teamwork Vine

pages.text: A huge berry grew at the very top of the tallest tree. Sharing Squirrel tried to reach it alone but couldn't. Brave Bear tried too — still too high!
pages.narratorLine: Some things are too big to do alone, and that's okay!

pages.text: 'What if we work together?' asked Squirrel. Bear stood strong while Squirrel climbed on his shoulders. Dog steadied them both. Deer cheered them on.
pages.narratorLine: Everyone has something to offer a team.

pages.text: They reached the berry together! And when they shared it, it tasted even sweeter. A vine grew down the tree with berries for everyone. 'Teamwork made more than we ever could alone,' said Bear.
pages.narratorLine: Who can you team up with today?

doAction.instruction: Do something together with someone — as a team!
steps: Pick a task: clean up, build something, or make something.
Invite someone to help you — or offer to help them.
Work together and celebrate what you made!

shinePrompt: What did you and your team accomplish together?
